newsitem.title: USA: NYS comptroller raises concerns over Pataki budget.
newsitem.headline: NYS comptroller raises concerns over Pataki budget.

text.p: The New York State Comptroller on Tuesday said Gov. George Pataki's proposed budget for fiscal 1998 included some troubling debt-financing proposals.

"The governor's capital plan proposes to decrease pay-as- you-go capital financing from 37 percent to 21 percent by increasing back-door borrowing. As a result, state debt service will grow to more than 10 percent of the budget within three years," said Comptroller H. Carl McCall.

McCall, a Democrat, also said he doubted one of the chief claims of the Republican governor's administration -- that the proposed budget would reduce spending from General Fund, funded by taxpayers, to $32.83 billion.
"It appears, on initial analysis, that general fund spending will actually increase this year by $54 million rather than decrease by $56 million as the governor claims," McCall said.
He said his staff would conduct a thorough review of the governor's budget and disclose the results in three weeks.
McCall added he was concerned about the use of a surplus, estimated by Pataki at $1.3 billion in fiscal 1997, ending March 31, to help narrow the next year's budget gap to about $1.3 billion.

He added that Pataki's move to raise school aid by $1.7 billion over five years was below the historical rate of such spending gains, and cautioned that the state could not continue to rely upon another booming year for Wall Street.

The state comptroller urged the governor to do more to increase employment and address property tax reform, reiterating that the state ranks 49th in creating jobs. While New York is 26th in state taxes, it remains the nation's leader in local taxes "by a wide margin," he said.
